title: Raising capital and surviving a downturn: Jason Calacanis on runway, cuts, and investor pitches
summary: Recorded in the early 2020 COVID crisis, Jason Calacanis gives a wartime playbook: be honest about the business, get to 18 months of runway, cut fast, and take services revenue to survive. He also covers pitching investors in a down market, valuation resets, cheap pivot tests and remote demos.

principles.text: Aim for 18 months of runway in a downturn; with six months of cash you will probably die unless you act.
principles.quote: you're gonna need eighteen months of cash that's the bottom line if you have six months of cash you're probably gonna die if you don't do anything

principles.text: Make the cuts and extend runway before you pitch; investors back founders who have already landed the plane.
principles.quote: after you've done all the necessary work of making the cuts extending the runway and driving revenue as best as you can that's a good time to go talk to investors

principles.text: In a crisis revenue is revenue: take services or consulting work from customers to survive, even at lower margin.
principles.quote: revenue is revenue if you can get revenue in the door through services yeah it's not the same margin but you got to eat

principles.text: Expect valuations to roughly halve in a down market, and don't be precious about price or round size.
principles.quote: I would say half of what the current market rate is and for YC companies maybe a third

principles.text: Don't spin your numbers; show raw weekly or monthly revenue and be candid about what works and what doesn't.
principles.quote: don't spin it's it's really a wasted thing if you spin this stuff we find out anyway and then you look like you're you know playing games

principles.text: Test a pivot with the laziest, cheapest experiment: a landing page that takes a credit card before you build anything.
principles.quote: that's how you do proper pivoting is what's the least amount of work what's the smallest test the most efficient test I can do the laziest way to get an answer to my question
